WearTrailsExperiments Web experiments JavaScriptthree.jsAmmo.jsWebGLglTF / GLB WearTrailsExperiments gathers browser prototypes that turn the contact between a sliding body and the ground into persistent wear and flow maps. They explore, in JavaScript, the idea behind the ÉTS master’s research on wear in texture space: contact patches, tangential velocity and traction written into a texture where contact actually happened. The repository is published under ETSim for graphics researchers who want to try those ideas without building a native simulator.
Overview There are two parts.
docs/, the modular application. docs/index.html loads three.js 0.158 and Ammo.js from a CDN and starts js/main-clean-complete.js. A body (cube, soft volumetric cube, sphere, torus puck, cylinder puck, cone or custom GLB) is dropped on a plane with chosen gravity, friction, restitution, speed and force. Each frame:
js/contacts.js samples contact points and their centre; js/bounding-box/ fits the contact patch with AABB, PCA-based OBB, rotating-calipers OMBB, KDOP-8 or a hybrid method; js/pip/ renders eight picture-in-picture views: top, bottom and intersection masks, tangential velocity, instant traction (τ = μ σn), accumulated sliding distance, local sliding distance with direction vectors, and local wear; js/managers/flow-accumulation-manager.js accumulates wear as K × traction × velocity on the ground, keeps a time-smoothed sliding direction and encodes both as HSVA or RGBA; js/managers/ground-variant-manager.js loads a GLB ground with material variants and blends them with the wear map, rotating textures along the flow direction; js/shaders/wear-map-shader.js colours the sliding-distance map with optional logarithmic scaling. experiments/, single-file prototypes. Nine standalone HTML pages named after their content: contact masks, dynamic paint with UV trails and OBB hulls, slip vector fields, multi-layer paint with GLB support, directional and hardness-based wear simulations, and GLB/flow-field blending. docs/glb_khr_variants_blend.html is a smaller test of blending glTF material variants with a grayscale map.
Getting started The pages use ES modules, so they need a local web server. From the README in docs/:
cd docs python -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 Click Start, adjust the controls in the left panel and watch the PiP views. Pause, Step Frame and Apply Angular Impulse help follow one contact, and Export Wear Map or Save Stamps save the ground maps as PNG. The pages in experiments/ open the same way. An internet connection is required for the CDN libraries.
Repository guide docs/index.html is the main application page with its control panel. docs/js/main-clean-complete.js is the entry module. docs/js/main.js is an alternative entry module that index.html does not load. docs/js/bodies/ creates the physics bodies, docs/js/body-manager.js handles their lifecycle. docs/js/bounding-box/ holds the contact-patch fitting algorithms. docs/js/pip/ holds the eight picture-in-picture renderers. docs/js/managers/ holds the scene, physics, ground, stamping, field/flow, wear accumulation and GLB variant managers. docs/js/shaders/wear-map-shader.js is the GLSL wear-map shader. experiments/ holds the standalone HTML prototypes. Features Rigid and soft bodies on Ammo.js physics, including custom GLB models. Five contact-patch fitting methods, with velocity-based OBB alignment. Live views of contact masks, tangential velocity, traction, sliding distance and wear. Persistent wear accumulation on the ground, cleared only on demand, with a time-smoothed sliding direction. GLB material-variant blending driven by accumulated wear. PNG export of stamps, wear and flow maps. Limits These are research prototypes: the wear model is a visual heuristic in canvas buffers, not a calibrated tribology model. docs/README.md describes an older layout (stamp/, field-flow/, six PiP views) that no longer matches the files, and the top-level README is one sentence. Libraries are loaded from CDNs, including Ammo.js from a moving branch (@HEAD or @main) in several pages, so results can change without a code change. Most experiments use three.js 0.160 while the application uses 0.158. The README notes that the OBB angle can jitter at low speed and that custom GLB models should be convex. There are no tests or build step. Sources GitHub repository README docs/README.md docs/js/main-clean-complete.js docs/js/managers/flow-accumulation-manager.js docs/js/managers/ground-variant-manager.js
summary: three.js and Ammo.js experiments that turn rigid-body contact, traction and sliding into wear, sliding-distance and flow maps on a ground texture.
title: WearTrailsExperiments: contact-driven wear trails in the browser

BatchBacktesting BatchBacktesting turns a backtest into a repeatable batch: choose instruments, obtain and clean prices, run a strategy, and save comparable results. It is an AlgoÉTS repository; the facts below come from its source files and README as read for the companion article.
Overview Why it exists. A batch backtest is a small data pipeline, and the project keeps every step visible in Python instead of behind a dashboard.
Best fit. Comparing one strategy across many instruments with the same recorded assumptions, then reading the per-instrument and aggregate CSVs side by side.
Getting started The README links a published example rather than a one-command install; the runner is the entry point.
Runner: src/BatchBacktesting.py — process_instrument selects a stock or crypto price adapter, cleans the data and constructs a Backtest. Strategies: src/strategies.py. Analysis helpers: src/analyse.py. Published AAPL EMA chart (2018-04-04 to 2023-04-03): output/charts/EMA. Features and components Component What it does Instrument runner Picks the price adapter, cleans observations, runs one Backtest, tags the result with instrument and strategy names Worker pool ThreadPoolExecutor, four workers by default for the single-strategy runner; the multi-strategy helper nests an outer pool around inner pools Strategy defaults 100,000 starting cash, 0.002 commission (0.2%), exclusive orders EMA strategy 20-, 80- and 150-period EMAs computed; entries compare the 20 and 80 curves; long side closes the prior position and buys with a 90% stop and a 125% target Outputs Per-instrument CSV, aggregate CSV per strategy, optional HTML chart Architecture flowchart TD I["Instrument list and strategy"] --> P["ThreadPoolExecutor"] P --> D["Fetch and clean historical data"] D --> B["Backtest per instrument"] B --> R["Result with Instrument and Strategy"] R --> C["Per-instrument CSV"] R --> A["Aggregate strategy CSV"] B --> H["Optional HTML chart"] Constraints and checks A failed instrument returns None; if every instrument fails, the later concatenation has no frames. groupby("Instrument").max() in analyse.py takes each column’s maximum independently, so a summary row can mix metrics from different runs. Select a real row by return before quoting its drawdown. The defaults do not cover slippage, short availability, delisted securities or corporate actions. Worker counts and dates above are code defaults and example dates, not measured throughput or a fixed range. Links Repository Published example Workshop1, the beginner notebooks that lead into this batch runner

MistubaVideo MistubaVideo renders simulation exports with Mitsuba 3, under ETSim. The batch command processes OBJ sequences; the mitsuba-video helper reads recorded body poses and surface fields through manifest and TextureFriction source adapters. Facts below come from the repository documentation as read for the project introduction.
Overview Why it exists. A simulation computes motion and surface change; rendering a recording shows where bodies moved and how material appearance evolved, and lets you change camera or lighting without repeating the simulation.
Best fit. Turning recorded poses and wear fields into frames, heatmaps, atlas panels and video for reports and talks.
Getting started python main.py multi --folder exports # batch-render an OBJ sequence mitsuba-video inspect path/to/manifest.json # check the input data mitsuba-video preview path/to/manifest.json # check camera and framing mitsuba-video render path/to/manifest.json -q preview Quality presets: preview, draft, paper. encode reassembles existing frames into video; FFmpeg does the encoding.
Features and components Stage Data Input Meshes, materials, recorded poses and surface fields; a versioned manifest (bodies, meshes, materials, poses, field images) or a TextureFriction recording through a source adapter; ManifestWriter lets another simulator export the format Processing Apply recorded poses, blend base and affected materials using the surface field, Mitsuba 3 path tracing; optional heatmap, UV-atlas panel and covered-area chart Output Beauty and composite frames, field-area CSV, render_config.json with settings and timings, MP4; optional linear EXR frames Architecture flowchart TD subgraph Inputs[Simulation output] R[TextureFriction recording] M[Manifest: meshes, poses and fields] end subgraph Helper[mitsuba-video helper] A[Source adapter] B[Apply poses and blend materials] C[Mitsuba 3 path tracing] D[Atlas panel and area chart] end R --> A M --> A A --> B --> C --> D D --> E[Frame images and MP4] Constraints and checks The area chart measures the recorded field’s covered area, not the visible area of the rendered object. Keep display settings with the render: changing the heatmap range makes the same field look different. The package documents pytest tests for transforms, material blending, OBJ/MTL readers and the manifest schema and writer; no measured coverage percentage is quoted here. TrueMapData TrueMapData is a Python library and tmd-process CLI for TrueMap and GelSight height maps, maintained under ETSim. It reads surface captures as NumPy arrays and provides analysis and graphics export. Facts below come from the repository README and guides as read for the companion article.
Overview Why it exists. One surface representation that serves metrology work and graphics assets such as displacement maps or meshes.
Best fit. Inspecting measured surfaces, comparing captures over time (wear), and exporting normal maps, displacement maps or meshes with physical scale preserved.
Getting started pip install "truemapdata[viz]" tmd-process visualize basic path/to/capture.tmd tmd-process visualize 3d path/to/capture.tmd --plotter plotly --output surface.html from tmd import TMD capture = TMD.load("path/to/capture.tmd") heights = capture.height_map metadata = capture.metadata Paths are placeholders. Optional extras: truemapdata[roughness] (Surfalize, GPL-3.0, installed separately from the MIT core) and the mesh dependencies for STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF and USD export.
Features and components Area Content File format .tmd header, spatial metadata and a float32 row-major height grid; legacy v1 and TrueMap v6-style v2 formats, with checks for alternate v2 headers Visualisation 2D heatmap, 3D surface, row and column profiles, contours, file comparisons; Matplotlib, Plotly HTML, optional Polyscope Derived maps Normal maps, displacement maps, apply-on-mesh with a template OBJ/MTL using template bounds, mm_per_pixel and capture dimensions for tiling Metrology ISO 25178 areal roughness through Surfalize (optional) Wear tmd-wear commands: volume series, scratch evolution, slip-axis heuristics, roughness trajectories; translation alignment and OpenCV/SIFT registration, including normals-driven registration Pipeline tools Filters, defect detection, sequence export, compression Architecture flowchart TB Capture["TrueMap or GelSight capture"] --> Read["Height grid and spatial metadata"] Read --> Inspect["Heatmap, profile or 3D surface"] Inspect --> Metrics["Roughness and surface metrics"] Inspect --> Maps["Normal and displacement maps"] Inspect --> Mesh["Mesh export and template texturing"] Constraints and checks Roughness describes one capture; wear compares captures over time and needs the same grid and in-plane region before heights are subtracted. Loss convention: reference height − current height; positive loss means the current surface is lower. Physical volume also needs the pixel spacing in both directions. Registration errors or inconsistent height units change wear results. The README figures are repository examples with normalised heights, not thesis measurements. Links Repository Documentation Binary format guide · Sequential wear analysis MistubaVideo renders the recorded surface fields this tooling measures
summary: TrueMapData reads TrueMap and GelSight height maps, processes them and exports visual, surface and mesh-oriented results.

Workshop1 Workshop1 is an AlgoÉTS notebook-based Python workshop. The sequence moves from setup through API calls, pandas and visualisation, and ends with an Apple-price EMA exercise. Facts below come from the repository as read for the companion article.
Overview Why it exists. A beginner workshop where each new concept has somewhere to go: a request becomes a table, the table becomes a chart.
Best fit. First contact with Python for finance students, before moving to a batch experiment such as BatchBacktesting.
Getting started Open the first notebook in Colab: 1.1_python_basic.ipynb (linked from the README). Or clone the repository and run local Jupyter; the setup notebooks cover the environment. API availability, keys and package versions can change since the original workshop. The notebooks are teaching material to inspect and adapt.
Features and components Nine Jupyter notebooks across six numbered directories:
Stage Notebooks Environment and cloud setup 2 Python basics and advanced concepts 2 Reading API responses 1 Cleaning and exploring with pandas 1 Visualisation 2 Final project 1 — 5.1_project_ema.ipynb plots Apple closing prices with 12-, 26-, 50-, 100- and 200-day EMA curves These are counts of checked-in material, not attendance or completion statistics.
Architecture flowchart TD S["Environment and cloud notebooks"] --> P["Python basics and advanced concepts"] P --> A["Read API responses"] A --> D["Clean and explore with pandas"] D --> V["Visualize the data"] V --> E["Apple prices and EMA project"] Constraints and checks The final exercise connects a request, tabular data, indicator columns and a labelled chart. It does not establish that any crossover is profitable. Classroom checks worth keeping: ordered dates, intentional handling of missing values, why a longer EMA responds more slowly, and whether every curve uses the same observations. Install the vimrc setup DeveloperUpstream projects install_vimrc in install.sh installs vim and git, clones amix/vimrc into ~/.vim_runtime and runs its installer; edit_vimrc moves NERDTree to the left and turns on line numbers.
Set up Oh My Zsh and tmux DeveloperUpstream projects install_oh_my_zsh downloads the official Oh My Zsh installer with wget; edit_oh_my_zsh switches the theme and writes a minimal prompt theme; install_tmux writes a full ~/.tmux.conf.
Install dev toolchains DeveloperOS package manager bash install.sh <option> runs one installer (Python, JDK, nvm, .NET, Go, Rust, Docker, kubectl, AWS CLI, Azure CLI, JupyterLab, network tools); install_package reads /etc/os-release to pick apt-get, pacman, dnf, yum or brew.

Remove tools with backups DeveloperOS package manager uninstall.sh copies ~/.vimrc and ~/.tmux.conf to .backup files before deleting them, and purges JDK, Python, Rust, Go, Jupyter, AWS CLI, Azure CLI and nvm; run with bash, it calls every uninstall function in turn.
Show neofetch at login DeveloperOS package manager motd/motd.sh installs neofetch with apt-get when missing and writes /etc/update-motd.d/10-neofetch so the system summary appears in the login banner.

Use-case diagram for another-install-script: Install base server tools; Deploy selected containers; Open ports for containers; Remove installed containers; Uninstall the setup another-install-script Install base server tools Deploy selected containers Open ports for containers Remove installed containers Uninstall the setup Server admin «system» Docker Engine «system» UFW firewall People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Install base server tools Server admin The Installation entry of main_setup_menu (src/menu.sh) shows a checklist: basic packages, Docker, Cockpit, LXDE, Ansible, Dokku, Vagrant and more; src/install.sh runs the selected items.
Deploy selected containers Server adminDocker Engine Add Container lists the folders under containers/; each <name>.sh runs docker-compose up -d on the docker-compose.yml next to it (for example containers/gogs/).
Open ports for containers Server adminUFW firewall After containers are added, manage_firewall_ports_allow_list in src/firewall.sh reads their ports from config.yml and allows them; with system.firewall set to yes, ufw denies other incoming traffic but keeps SSH, 2222, HTTP and HTTPS.
Remove installed containers Server adminDocker Engine remove_container_menu shows the installed containers; each remove_docker_<name> function runs docker-compose down on that service.
Uninstall the setup Server adminDocker EngineUFW firewall The Uninstall entry runs uninstall.sh, which loads the src/ modules to undo the setup. The Backup entry currently calls the same script; the backup helpers in src/backup.sh are not wired to the menu.
Scenario: Provision a new VPS with a few self-hosted services Clone the repository and run sudo bash setup.sh; it opens main_setup_menu because bashmenu is yes in config.yml.Choose Installation and keep basic and docker checked; selecting docker opens the container list next.Tick services such as gogs and bookstack; each script runs docker-compose up -d.Let the firewall step allow the ports listed in config.yml and enable ufw.Later, use Remove Container to stop a service with docker-compose down. Use cases Moonlight Embedded fork that streams games from a Sunshine PC to a New 3DS, with a bottom-screen helper UI.

Install the CIA or 3DSX 3DS player dist/INSTALL.md describes installing artemis.cia from the HOME Menu with FBI, or copying artemis.3dsx to sd:/3ds/artemis/ for the Homebrew Launcher; custom firmware is required.
Pair with a host 3DS playerSunshine host PC The player adds a host by LAN IP (host_discovery.cpp can also scan the network) and chooses pair; pair_host in src/n3ds_main.cpp shows a PIN to type into Sunshine and keeps a pair record.
Stream a game or desktop 3DS playerSunshine host PC Video plays on the top screen using the New 3DS hardware H.264 decoder; older 3DS models fall back to software decode at lower frame rates, per the README.
Switch touch input modes 3DS playerSunshine host PC The SELECT hub on the bottom screen switches between gamepad, mouse, keyboard, magnify and mirror handlers in src/input/touch/, plus Fit, Fill, Stretch and zoom display options.
Save performance as CSV 3DS player From the Session tab, the performance overlay shows stream telemetry; export_stream_benchmark_csv in src/stream_benchmark.cpp writes benchmark_<time>.csv to the SD card.
Build with devkitPro Developer docker build of the Dockerfile gives a devkitPro image; make inside it produces artemis.3dsx, artemis.cia and artemis.elf. A local devkitPro 3ds-dev setup with bannertool and makerom also works.

Tune video presentation Switch player Fit, Fill, Stretch, Zoom/Pan, rotation and full range share one deko3d presentation path, with FSR/EASU upscaling, RCAS sharpening and dithering on top of NVDEC decode.
Save stream profiles Switch playerGameStream host PC Named profiles store FPS (30 to 120), resolution, bitrate, codec and presentation in profile.json; they can be assigned per host, edited and imported or exported (StreamProfileStore.cpp, ProfileEditorDialog.cpp).
Export a benchmark Switch player The Performance page shows bitrate, latency, frame queue, GPU time and Switch clocks; Benchmark start, stop and save write a file through app/src/benchmark/BenchmarkExport.cpp.
Build and test the app Developer With devkitA64 and CMake, the Moonlight.nro target builds the Switch binary, exported by CI as Artemis-Switch.nro; tests/ holds portable unit tests run with ctest, plus Python i18n and release checks.

Overview Why it exists Audio ingestion and transcription worker pipeline with timestamp alignment.
Best fit Batch automated audio recording transcription and indexing.
Use cases Python CLI that splits a WAV file on silence and transcribes each chunk into a single text.
Use-case diagram for AudioTranscript: Split audio on silence; Transcribe the chunks; Set AWS keys in .env; Try Whisper on a sample AudioTranscript Split audio on silence Transcribe the chunks Set AWS keys in .env Try Whisper on a sample CLI user «system» Amazon Transcribe «system» Hugging Face Hub People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Split audio on silence CLI user main.py loads the WAV with pydub and calls split_on_silence with --min-silence-len, --silence-thresh (relative to the file’s dBFS) and --keep-silence, writing each piece to audio-chunks/chunkN.wav.
Transcribe the chunks CLI userAmazon Transcribe Each chunk goes to recognize_amazon (us-east-1, S3 bucket from .env) and the texts are joined and printed. The README describes Google Speech Recognition, but the code calls Amazon; the --language option is not passed on.
Set AWS keys in .env CLI userAmazon Transcribe load_dotenv reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_BUCKET_NAME; main.py raises an error if one is missing.
Try Whisper on a sample CLI userHugging Face Hub ai.py is a separate script that loads openai/whisper-large-v2 with transformers and transcribes one LibriSpeech dummy sample; it is not wired to the CLI and its packages are not in requirements.txt.
Scenario: Transcribe a recorded interview Run pip install -r requirements.txt, plus python-dotenv, which main.py imports but the file does not list.Create a .env file with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_BUCKET_NAME.Run python main.py interview.wav -m 700 -s -16 (the path is positional and defaults to caro.wav).main.py writes the chunks to audio-chunks/ and shows a Rich progress bar.Each chunk is sent to Amazon Transcribe and the full text is printed at the end. Features and components 2 Audio segmentation main.py loads a WAV through pydub and calls split_on_silence. The threshold is calculated relative to the recording’s dBFS level. Each chunk is exported to audio-chunks before recognition. Recognition and output A SpeechRecognition Recognizer reads each exported file and calls recognize_amazon. The loop appends the returned text to whole_text, which is printed and returned. Typer exposes the file and segmentation parameters. Register an account Registered user RegisteredUserController stores a new user with email, username, phone and password; the form is resources/js/Pages/Auth/Register.tsx.
Log in with throttling Registered userAdministrator LoginRequest locks an email and IP pair after 5 failed attempts and records login_attempts, browser, OS, IP and last_login on the user row.
Reset a forgotten password Registered userMailpit (dev mail) The forgot-password routes send a reset link by email; in the Sail stack, Mailpit catches it and shows it on port 8025.
Change profile and password Registered user PUT /password goes to PasswordController, and /profile lets the user edit, update or delete the account through ProfileController.

Overview Why it exists Full-featured web control interface for Chitubox SDCP 3.0 resin printers with LAN UDP discovery.
Best fit Headless remote management and real-time print monitoring for SLA 3D printers.
Use cases Flask web UI that finds Chitubox SDCP 3.0 resin printers on the LAN, uploads files and starts prints.
Use-case diagram for ChitUI: Discover printers on the LAN; Watch printer status; Upload a print file; List and delete files; Start a print ChitUI Discover printers on the LAN Watch printer status Upload a print file List and delete files Start a print Printer operator «system» SDCP resin printer People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Discover printers on the LAN Printer operatorSDCP resin printer At start-up, discover_printers in main.py broadcasts M99999 over UDP port 3000, saves the replies and opens a WebSocket to each printer at ws://<ip>:3030/websocket.
Watch printer status Printer operatorSDCP resin printer The browser asks over Socket.IO; main.py sends SDCP commands 0 (status) and 1 (attributes) and relays printer messages to web/js/chitui.js and sdcp.js.
Upload a print file Printer operatorSDCP resin printer POST /upload accepts .ctb, .goo and .prz files, computes an MD5 and sends 1 MB parts to http://<ip>:3030/uploadFile/upload; /progress streams the percentage.
List and delete files Printer operatorSDCP resin printer printer_files sends SDCP command 258 with a storage path; action_delete sends command 259 with the file list.
Start a print Printer operatorSDCP resin printer action_print sends SDCP command 128 with the file name and StartLayer 0.
Scenario: Send a sliced model to a resin printer from a browser Install requirements.txt in a virtualenv and run python main.py, or use docker run --net=host so UDP broadcast works.At start-up, ChitUI broadcasts M99999 on UDP port 3000 and connects to each printer’s WebSocket on port 3030.Open http://127.0.0.1:54780/ to see the discovered printers and their status.Upload a .ctb file; ChitUI saves it to /tmp and sends it in 1 MB parts with an MD5 check.Pick the file in the printer’s file list and start the print. Save a diagram to ComfyUI ComfyUI user The viewer’s Save button posts to /comfyui-uml/save, registered with the other routes in nodes/uml_routes.py.

Sign in to the dashboard Homelab adminPostgreSQL cargo run --bin create_admin creates the first account; POST /tenants/api/login checks the bcrypt hash and returns a JWT used by the protected routes.

Save and switch workspaces Homelab adminPostgreSQL The /workspaces/api routes create, update, list and delete workspaces and their applets, stored in PostgreSQL through Diesel.
Stop or restart containers Homelab adminDocker Engine /containers/api/docker_list lists containers through shiplift, and /containers/api/stop/<id> and restart/<id> act on one container when a valid token is sent.
Open a web SSH terminal Homelab admin src/bin/start_websocket.rs bridges a WebSocket to an ssh2 session for the Terminal applet; the README lists the web terminal as in progress.

Compute with dense and sparse Rust developer The mathlib crate provides dense and sparse matrices, vectors, SVD and 3D helpers; cd mathlib && cargo test and cargo bench exercise them.
Render a 3D scene with wgpu Rust developerGPU via wgpu The render crate draws a mathlib Tree scene through wgpu; cargo run -p render-demo --example render_native opens a window with a cube, gizmo and picking.
Load meshes and data files Rust developer The parse crate reads JSON, XML, OBJ, MTL, BVH, glTF, PLY, PNG, JPEG, ZIP and TAR behind Cargo features such as json and obj.
Simulate physics, collisions Rust developer physics implements PBD/XPBD with examples particles_2d, rigid_bodies_3d and softbody_3d; collision adds AABB, OBB, BVH, BSP, ray and frustum queries.
Publish the WASM demo site Rust developerBrowser (WASM/WebGPU) just website-build compiles the mathlib, render, kinematics, physics, geometry and neural demos to WASM into website/; pages.yml deploys it to GitHub Pages.

Overview Why it exists Production MCP server connecting AI assistants to Quebec & Montreal open data APIs with strict schema validation.
Best fit Natural language querying of public municipal and provincial datasets across transportation, demographics, and municipal services.
Use cases An MCP server that lets AI agents search, query in SQL and map Québec and Montréal open data in conversation.
Use-case diagram for donneesqc-mcp: Search open datasets; Run read-only SQL queries; Find and query in one call; Explore geospatial layers; Geocode, convert coordinates donneesqc-mcp Search open datasets Run read-only SQL queries Find and query in one call Explore geospatial layers Geocode, convert coordinates Analyst with an agent «system» CKAN open data portals «system» IGO geo services People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Search open datasets Analyst with an agentCKAN open data portals search_datasets and search_montreal_datasets call the CKAN APIs of Données Québec and Montréal (DQ_API_URL, MTL_API_URL) through helpers/ckan_api.py.
Run read-only SQL queries Analyst with an agentCKAN open data portals query_resource_sql and query_montreal_sql send SQL to the CKAN DataStore after validate_sql() rejects anything that is not a SELECT.
Find and query in one call Analyst with an agentCKAN open data portals find_and_query chains search, resource listing and DataStore query so the agent avoids three round trips.
Explore geospatial layers Analyst with an agentIGO geo services list_geospatial_layers, get_geospatial_features and get_map_url query the IGO WFS and build WMS GetMap URLs through helpers/geo_api.py.
Geocode, convert coordinates Analyst with an agentIGO geo services geocode and reverse_geocode use the icherche geocoder (GEOCODER_URL); convert_coordinates switches between EPSG:32198 and EPSG:4326.
Scenario: Counting public trees per borough in Montréal Start the server with docker compose up -d (or uv sync then uv run python main.py); it listens on port 8000 with streamable HTTP.Register it in the client, for example claude mcp add --transport http donneesqc http://localhost:8000/mcp.Ask the agent for public tree data; it calls search_montreal_datasets to find the dataset.The agent calls query_montreal_data to see the columns of the DataStore resource.It sends a SELECT … GROUP BY query through query_montreal_sql and answers with the per-borough counts. Overview Why it exists Embedded microcontroller firmware and mobile controller for driving multi-digit 7-segment displays.
Best fit Physical computing status dashboards and hardware displays.
Use cases ESP32 firmware and an Android app that drive an I2C 7-segment display as a countdown or stopwatch over Wi-Fi.
Use-case diagram for ESP32-7SEG: Join the board to Wi-Fi; Start a countdown or stopwatch; Set the digits directly; Follow updates live; Control it from Android ESP32-7SEG Join the board to Wi-Fi Start a countdown or stopwatch Set the digits directly Follow updates live Control it from Android Timer operator «system» ESP32 + 7-seg display «system» Android app People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Join the board to Wi-Fi Timer operatorESP32 + 7-seg display Without saved credentials, wifi.cpp starts an access point named ESPTimer; the / page then serves the setup form, and POST /connect stores the SSID and password in NVS.
Start a countdown or stopwatch Timer operatorESP32 + 7-seg display POST /timer-action with action, mode, minutes and seconds starts, pauses or stops a FreeRTOS task (COUNTDOWN or STOPWATCH) in display.cpp.
Set the digits directly Timer operatorESP32 + 7-seg display POST /update-display with minutes and seconds calls updateDisplay() and pushes a displayUpdated message.
Follow updates live Android appESP32 + 7-seg display The /ws WebSocket broadcasts timerStarted, timerStopped and displayUpdated JSON; the Android WebSocketClient listens to it.
Control it from Android Timer operatorAndroid app TimerApiService.kt maps the same endpoints with Retrofit (/timer-action, /connect, /scan, /update-display, /device-info) behind the TimerControl and WiFiConnect fragments.
Scenario: Setting up a 5-minute countdown on a fresh board Wire the Adafruit I2C backpack to SDA, SCL, VCC and GND, then flash the firmware with pio run -t upload (env firebeetle).On first boot no credentials are in NVS, so join the ESPTimer access point and open the board's page.Pick a network from /scan and submit it to /connect; the board saves it and joins the LAN.Read the new IP in the serial monitor at 115200 baud and open it in a browser or the Android app.Send action=start, mode=countdown, minutes=5, seconds=0 to /timer-action; the display counts down and /ws reports each update. Pick a game from the list Player The #swfSelector drop-down in index.html lists Tag, Ricochet Kill and Ballon, each with a short description.
Play a SWF in the browser PlayerRuffle emulator loadSWF() creates a Ruffle player with RufflePlayer.newest() and loads tag.swf, ricochet kill.swf or jeux.swf into #swfContainer.
Open a game by URL hash Player updateHash() writes the game key into the URL hash, and the load and hashchange listeners reload that game, so a link like #tag opens it directly.
Run the collection locally PlayerRuffle emulator The README says to clone the repository and open index.html; Ruffle is loaded from unpkg, so a network connection is still needed.
Scenario: Replaying Ricochet Kill from a shared link Open https://antoinebou12.github.io/FlashGames/ (or index.html from a clone).The page loads the first game, Tag, because no hash is set.Choose Ricochet Kill in the Select a Game list; the URL becomes #ricochet_kill.Ruffle loads ricochet kill.swf into the black game area and the description bar updates.Play with the mouse, then copy the URL to send someone straight to the same game. Overview Why it exists OpenCV color-keying pipeline converting chroma-key green videos to RGBA alpha PNG sequences.
Best fit Asset preparation for augmented reality (Snapchat Lens Studio, Spark AR).
Use cases A Python CLI that turns green-screen video into transparent PNG frames, GIFs or alpha .mov files for Lens Studio.
Use-case diagram for GreenScreenVideotoAlphaPNGs: Download footage from a URL; Split a video into frames; Key out the green background; Build a transparent GIF; Encode an alpha .mov GreenScreenVideotoAlphaPNGs Download footage from a URL Split a video into frames Key out the green background Build a transparent GIF Encode an alpha .mov AR lens creator «system» YouTube (yt-dlp) «system» ffmpeg People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Download footage from a URL AR lens creatorYouTube (yt-dlp) greenscreen convert accepts a YouTube URL; convert.py calls download_video() and download_audio() from download.py, which use yt-dlp.
Split a video into frames AR lens creatorffmpeg frames.py writes numbered PNGs (0.png, 1.png…) with ffmpeg, or with OpenCV when --no-ffmpeg is passed.
Key out the green background AR lens creator chroma.py computes a YCbCr distance from the key color (pixel 1,1 by default, tolerance 50–130) and writes RGBA PNGs into a sibling *_alpha folder.
Build a transparent GIF AR lens creatorffmpeg greenscreen gif <dir> uses numpngw and the optional APNGLib extension by default, or an ffmpeg palette with --fast-ffmpeg; the GIF is written next to the folder.
Encode an alpha .mov AR lens creatorffmpeg greenscreen video <dir> --fps 30 encodes the PNG sequence to Videogen-<stamp>.mov with the qtrle or prores_4444 codec.
Scenario: From a green-screen clip to a Lens Studio animation Run bash install.sh (or .\install.ps1 on Windows), then uv run greenscreen --help.Run uv run greenscreen convert clip.mp4 to extract frames into clip/ and keyed frames into clip_alpha/.Outputs that start with the clip name are moved into project_clip/ unless --no-project-dir is set.Run uv run greenscreen gif project_clip/clip_alpha --fast-ffmpeg to get a transparent GIF without APNGLib.In Lens Studio, use Resources → Add New → 2D animation from files and pick the *_alpha PNGs. python GreenVideotoAlphaPNGs.py → greenscreen convert python GIFGenerator.py → greenscreen gif python VideoGenerator.py → greenscreen video Read the full instructions ↗ Source documentation README.md 1 documents read from 1 candidates.
Features and components 2 Conversion stage The Typer convert command delegates to run_convert. It accepts a local video or URL and can prefer FFmpeg or force OpenCV extraction. The chroma module handles pixel transparency separately from acquisition. Encoding choices gif and video take a directory of PNG frames. The GIF path offers an FFmpeg palette option; video accepts qtrle or prores_4444. Encoding is a new stage, so frame rate and format can change without repeating acquisition. One update calls get_measurements, list_girth and list_girth_goal, then records the last-update time. Errors and sensor state The coordinator converts timeouts and API failures into UpdateFailed. Start X at depth 30 Display testerX server (Xorg) Xdepth.sh runs startx -- -depth 30 and prints the depth from xwininfo, falling back to depth 24; xorg.conf sets DefaultDepth 30.
Show a 10-bit gray gradient Display testerHDR10 monitor Viewer.py packs the RGB channels of images/gray_gradient_10.tiff into a cairo FORMAT_RGB30 surface and draws it in a GTK 3 window.
Compare 8-bit and 10-bit Display testerHDR10 monitor The images/ folder holds gray_gradient_8.tiff next to gray_gradient_10.tiff, so the same gradient can be viewed at both depths to compare banding by eye.

Features and components 2 Pixels and drawing imageio reads the source array. _draw_on allocates a packed buffer and shifts each channel according to the selected depth, then passes it to cairo.ImageSurface.create_for_data. Overview Why it exists Desktop Electron and TypeScript application orchestrating gaming library metadata and downloads.
Best fit Open-source alternative game launcher and library organizer.
Use cases A fork of Hydra Launcher, an Electron game library that downloads, launches, tracks playtime and syncs saves.
Use-case diagram for hydra: Build a game library; Download and queue games; Add download sources; Launch and track playtime; Back up saves to the cloud; Unlock achievements hydra Build a game library Download and queue games Add download sources Launch and track playtime Back up saves to the cloud Unlock achievements Player «system» Hydra API and Cloud «system» Torrents and hosters People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Build a game library PlayerHydra API and Cloud IPC handlers in src/main/events/library (add-game-to-library, add-custom-game-to-library, assign-game-to-collection) manage the local library; catalogue events fetch game details and artwork.
Download and queue games PlayerTorrents and hosters Torrent downloads run in python_rpc/main.py with libtorrent, while services/hosters handles direct hosts such as Gofile, Mediafire and Pixeldrain; torrenting events manage the queue.
Add download sources PlayerTorrents and hosters download-sources events add, remove and sync the source lists that feed download options for each game.
Launch and track playtime Player process-watcher.ts scans running processes against known executables to record playtime; on Linux, umu.ts and wine-prefix.ts prepare Proton or Wine.
Back up saves to the cloud PlayerHydra API and Cloud Ludusavi.backupGame() runs the bundled ludusavi binary to collect save files, and the cloud-save services upload, compare and restore them with Hydra Cloud.
Unlock achievements PlayerHydra API and Cloud services/achievements finds and parses local achievement files, merges them with remote data and shows notifications.
Scenario: From catalogue page to a backed-up save Install Node.js with Yarn, Python 3.9+ (pip install -r requirements.txt) and Rust, then run yarn; postinstall builds hydra-native.Open a game in the catalogue and add it to the library.Pick a download option; the Python RPC process starts the torrent and the download page shows progress.Launch the game; the process watcher detects the executable and counts playtime.Close the game and sync the save; ludusavi backs up the files and the cloud-save service uploads them. Overview Why it exists Friction and contact physics toolkit for robust computer graphics and finite element simulation.
Best fit Nonlinear continuous contact mechanics in 3D physics engines.
Related articles & deep dives Deep-dive article → IPC Toolkit: collision and friction inside a simulation How IPC Toolkit supplies collision detection, distance derivatives and friction calculations to a simulation.
Use cases A C++ library with Python bindings for Incremental Potential Contact: contact barriers, CCD and friction for simulators.
Use-case diagram for ipc-toolkit: Build a collision mesh; Find contacts within dhat; Evaluate barrier, derivatives; Get a collision-free step size; Add anisotropic friction; Script it from Python ipc-toolkit Build a collision mesh Find contacts within dhat Evaluate barrier, derivatives Get a collision-free step size Add anisotropic friction Script it from Python Simulation developer «system» Host simulator People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Build a collision mesh Simulation developer ipc::CollisionMesh takes vertex, edge and face matrices (Eigen), as in the README quick start.
Find contacts within dhat Simulation developerHost simulator NormalCollisions::build() uses a broad phase (hash grid, LBVH, sweep and prune…) to collect primitive pairs closer than dhat.
Evaluate barrier, derivatives Simulation developerHost simulator BarrierPotential returns the energy, gradient and sparse Hessian that the host solver adds to its objective.
Get a collision-free step size Simulation developerHost simulator compute_collision_free_stepsize() runs continuous collision detection (Tight Inclusion by default, nonlinear and additive variants in src/ipc/ccd) between two vertex states.
Add anisotropic friction Simulation developerHost simulator FrictionPotential works on TangentialCollisions; smooth_mu.hpp adds elliptical anisotropic friction coefficients (commit Anisotropic friction #210).
Script it from Python Simulation developer pybind11 bindings under python/src expose the same API as ipctk (pip install ipctk), built when IPC_TOOLKIT_BUILD_PYTHON is ON.
Scenario: Adding contact to one implicit time step Install the bindings with pip install ipctk, or add the library to a CMake project.Create a CollisionMesh from the vertices, edges and faces of the scene.Build NormalCollisions with dhat = 1e-3 for the current positions.Add the BarrierPotential energy, gradient and Hessian to the solver's Newton system.Before accepting the Newton step, clamp it with compute_collision_free_stepsize so no surfaces cross. Overview Why it exists Ruby on Rails web platform featuring asynchronous OpenGraph metadata scrapers and card previews.

Share a link or a file Member LinksController#create saves a Link with title, url and description; the Link model also mounts a CarrierWave FileUploader, and /files/new reuses the same form.
Preview a shared page MemberEmbedly The feed and link views add embedly-card anchors, and application.js calls embedly('card', …) to render a preview card or tooltip.
Vote and comment on links Member PUT /links/:id/like and /dislike use acts_as_votable, and nested /links/:link_id/comments routes attach comments to a link.
Search links and users Member Link.search and User.search filter by title or name with LIKE; the feed is paginated five links per page with will_paginate, and user cards show an online indicator.
Manage content in /admin Administrator config/routes.rb mounts RailsAdmin at /admin, and the users table has an admin flag.

Overview Why it exists Structured prompt engineering framework and Python validator generating crisp, valid SVG illustrations from LLM responses.
Best fit Automated vector icon and diagram generation for design systems.
Use cases Python utilities and data for a text-to-SVG challenge: load prompts, check SVG rules, build and render shapes.
Use-case diagram for LLM2SVG: Load prompts and SVG samples; Validate SVG constraints; Extract terms from a prompt; Build SVG from primitives; Render SVG to PNG; Report on the SVG dataset LLM2SVG Load prompts and SVG samples Validate SVG constraints Extract terms from a prompt Build SVG from primitives Render SVG to PNG Report on the SVG dataset ML researcher «system» cairosvg renderer People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Load prompts and SVG samples ML researcher SVGDataLoader in utils/data_loader.py reads data/train/train.csv and data/test/test.csv and collects the SVG files stored under data/train/svg/<id>/; SVGDataset in utils/svg_dataset.py wraps them as a PyTorch Dataset.
Validate SVG constraints ML researcher SVGConstraints.validate_svg in utils/svg_constraints.py rejects files over 10,000 bytes and any element or attribute outside the allowlist, parsing with defusedxml.
Extract terms from a prompt ML researcher TextParser in utils/text_parser.py pulls colours, shapes, patterns, materials, clothing, landscape and architecture terms from a description and picks a primary category.
Build SVG from primitives ML researcher utils/svg_utils.py has helpers for rect, circle, ellipse, path, polygon, line and group elements, a colour palette generator, generate_shapes and optimize_svg to shorten numbers.
Render SVG to PNG ML researchercairosvg renderer svg_to_png in utils/svg_utils.py calls cairosvg.svg2png and either writes a file or returns PNG bytes.
Report on the SVG dataset ML researcher SVGAnalyzer in utils/svg_analyzer.py counts SVGs, measures their sizes, tallies elements, validates every file and plots a size histogram against the 10 KB limit.
Scenario: Check a set of candidate SVGs before submission Point SVGDataLoader at the local data/ folder (the default path is hard-coded to the author’s Windows drive).Read the prompts from data/train/train.csv, for example "a starlit night over snow-covered peaks".Run SVGAnalyzer.validate_all_svgs("train") to test every SVG under data/train/svg/ with SVGConstraints.Call generate_summary_report to get a table of sizes and inferred sources, then plot_svg_size_distribution.Render a passing SVG with svg_to_png to compare it with the prompt. Upload a music sheet Musician The React form in maestro-app/src/pages/MusicSheetUploadForm/MusicSheetUploadForm.tsx takes a dropped file and a MIDI file name, then useMaestroClient.ts checks GET /health before posting to /convert.
Set tempos per measure Musician The form keeps a list of tempo, measure and force entries (default 120 at measure 1) and sends it as the JSON field tempos.
Recognize notes with Audiveris Audiveris OMR engine POST /convert in ConvertController.java checks the file (10 MB limit, PDF/JPG/PNG signature) and AudiverisController.java runs Audiveris in batch mode to export a .mxl file.
Convert MusicXML to MIDI music21 (Python) backend/src/main/MxlToMidi.py loads the .mxl with music21, applies dynamics and the requested tempo marks, and writes the .mid file.
Download the MIDI file Musician The backend returns the .mid as an attachment and the frontend saves it with js-file-download; input and output folders are cleaned three seconds later.
Switch English or French Musician LanguageSwitcher.tsx toggles i18next between en-US and fr-CA, using the strings in maestro-app/public/locales/.

Get a stock price Game playerMarketWatch website MarketWatch.get_price in marketwatch/__init__.py fetches the stock page with httpx and reads the intraday price with BeautifulSoup; the README marks it as working with skip_login=True.
Buy, sell, short or cover Game playerMarketWatch website buy, sell, short and cover build an order payload and submit it to a game; MarketWatchGame in marketwatch/game.py binds the same calls to one game ID.
Read portfolio and orders Game playerMarketWatch website get_portfolio, get_positions, get_pending_orders, get_leaderboard and get_game_settings scrape game pages; cancel_order and cancel_all_orders remove pending orders.
Manage watchlists Game playerMarketWatch website create_watchlist, add_to_watchlist, get_watchlists, delete_watchlist and delete_watchlist_item call the MarketWatch watchlist endpoints.
Serve HTML game cards Game playerMarketWatch website api/app.py is a FastAPI app with HTTP Basic auth that renders Jinja2 templates for /game, /portfolio, /leaderboard, /card and /watchlist.
Trade on an EMA crossover GitHub ActionsMarketWatch website .github/workflows/ema-workflow.yml runs on a five-minute cron, pulls prices with yfinance, computes 20 and 80 period EMAs and buys or sells 100 shares on a crossover.

Automate media downloads Homelab adminDocker host Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Bazarr handle TV, movies, music and subtitles, fed by Jackett, Prowlarr or NZBHydra2 and sent to Deluge or NZBGet, all under ${ROOT}.
Watch or request media Media viewerDocker host Plex (port 32400) and Jellyfin (port 8096) serve the library; Ombi and Jellyseerr take requests and Tautulli reports Plex activity.
Monitor and browse the host Homelab adminDocker host Netdata (port 19999) shows host metrics, FileBrowser gives web file access and Dashmachine (port 5000) is a start page configured by dashmachine/config.ini.
Publish services via Caddy Homelab admin caddy/Caddyfile maps subdomains such as sonarr.{$DOMAIN} to local ports with logging, rate limiting, an IP allowlist and basic auth taken from caddy/.env.
Add optional extras Homelab adminDocker host Separate compose files under extra/ add Samba shares, a WireGuard access server and Portainer; whisper/docker-compose.yml runs a Whisper ASR web service on port 9000.

Define entry and exit rules Strategy developer A strategy subclasses BackTest and fills build_indicators, entry_strategy (entry_signal, take_profit, stop_loss, position_size) and exit_strategy (exit_signal).
Run the backtest Strategy developer run_backtest simulates positions per pair with exchange fees, a maximum number of positions and a maximum holding time, then plots cumulative profit.
Save performance statistics Strategy developer The run writes results/<strategy>_pairs_stats.csv and results/<strategy>_overall_stats.json with returns, drawdown and per-pair figures.
Build indicator features Strategy developer TechnicalIndicatorsCreation in novalabs-backtest/utils/indicators.py adds lags, close ratios and support or resistance levels to a candle DataFrame.

Development and contributions Nova Backtest README.md
NovaLabs backtest is a Python library for backtesting algorithmic trading strategies. It aims to facilitate the development of algorithmic trading on the crypto market by downloading historical data prices on the biggest centralized exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX, KuCoin & more) and simulates the trades of a given strategy throughout past years. It returns a bunch of statistics, giving a strong evaluation of your strategies performances. Read the full instructions ↗ Source documentation README.mddocs/source/installation.rst 2 documents read from 2 candidates.
Features and components 2 Inputs and clients BackTest receives exchange, strategy name, candle interval, pair list and start/end times. It constructs a client through the clients factory and loads the exchange fee assumptions from FEES. Simulation state The constructor stores initial and current bankroll, leverage, maximum positions and holding duration. Geometric sizing is an explicit option. Reports depend on these assumptions as well as the strategy’s signals. Architecture Expand a component to follow its connections, or explore the full diagram.

Best fit Detailed gameplay analytics and playtime tracking for Switch homebrew.

View all-time playtime Switch playerSwitch PDM service The All Activity screen lists each game's total playtime, launch count, first and last launch, sorted by the chosen criterion; totals come from the system PDM statistics.
Graph recent play sessions Switch playerSwitch PDM service PlayData::readPlayDataFromPdm pages through pdmqryQueryPlayEvent; RecentActivity and Details draw a graph by day, month or year and list each play session.
Export or import play data Switch player Settings runs ExportJob to write /switch/NX-Activity-Log/export.json and ImportJob to read import.json into importedData.json, matched by username.
Customize the theme Switch player CustomTheme and ColourPicker let the player change every colour; a PNG at /config/NX-Activity-Log/background.png sets a custom background.
Update from inside the app Switch playerGitHub Releases UpdateUtils.cpp queries the GitHub API for the latest antoinebou12/NX-Activity-Log release and downloads its first asset with curl.
Replace the User Page Switch player Forwarder/ is a modified nx-hbloader that opens the app from the User Page; the README warns this mode is unreliable on HOS 21 and later.

Overview Why it exists Cellular automaton sand physics simulation engine running on libnx with touch and controller input.
Best fit Interactive physics simulations on handheld console touchscreens.
Use cases Falling-sand sandbox for Nintendo Switch homebrew, simulated on the GPU with OpenGL ES 3.0, with desktop builds.
Use-case diagram for nxsand: Paint materials on the grid; Watch materials react; Save and load worlds; Tune performance settings; Import a Powder Toy stamp; Build and test the NRO nxsand Paint materials on the grid Watch materials react Save and load worlds Tune performance settings Import a Powder Toy stamp Build and test the NRO Player Homebrew developer «system» GPU (OpenGL ES 3.0) People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Paint materials on the grid PlayerGPU (OpenGL ES 3.0) Touch, Joy-Con or mouse input becomes brush strokes (source/sim/brush_stroke.cpp) written into the grid by shaders/paint.frag; the X button opens the material ring (source/ui/material_wheel.cpp).
Watch materials react PlayerGPU (OpenGL ES 3.0) A Margolus cellular automaton runs on ping-pong GL_R8UI textures in shaders/sim.frag or sim.comp, with reactions such as lava plus water giving stone in shaders/sim_common.glsl and the sim_rules_body.glsl it includes.
Save and load worlds Player source/save/save.cpp stores up to three slots as JSON with base64 grids in sdmc:/switch/nxsand/ (./nxsand_save/ on desktop); Y or F5 quick-saves.
Tune performance settings PlayerGPU (OpenGL ES 3.0) settings.json and the Engine menu set sim resolution, substeps, active tiles, fragment or compute backend and the Battery Saver, Balanced or Quality presets.
Import a Powder Toy stamp Homebrew developer nx::importTptStampJson in source/save/tpt_stamp_import.cpp maps The Powder Toy element IDs to NXSand materials and scales the stamp into the grid.
Build and test the NRO Homebrew developer make builds build/NXSand.nro with devkitPro; make desktop and make test build the SDL2 desktop version and the CPU reference tests in tests/; CI does the same in .github/workflows/native-nro.yml.
Scenario: Build NXSand and play a first world Install devkitPro, then run dkp-pacman -S switch-dev switch-sdl2 switch-mesa switch-glm switch-freetype switch-harfbuzz.Run make at the repository root to get build/NXSand.nro.Copy it to sdmc:/switch/NXSand.nro and launch it from the Homebrew Menu.Press X to pick Lava, paint with A, then switch to Water and pour it on the lava to see stone and smoke form.Press Y to quick-save the world into sdmc:/switch/nxsand/. NXSand ships as a homebrew .nro. You need a Switch setup that can run homebrew. For controls, settings, and architecture, see the full documentation site. Read the full instructions ↗ Install on Switch docs/INSTALL.md
Copy NXSand.nro to sdmc:/switch/NXSand.nro (required). Install NXSand.nsp with your CFW tool (Tinfoil, DBI, Goldleaf, etc.). Launch NXSand from the Home menu. If the forwarder fails, launch the .nro from the homebrew menu instead. Forwarders need a CFW setup that allows unsigned NSP installs. Keep prod.keys private; never commit them. Read the full instructions ↗ Operations and troubleshooting Troubleshooting docs/INSTALL.md
The app file must be sdmc:/switch/NXSand.nro, not inside the save folder. Build and deploy: powershell -File scripts\build-native.ps1 → copy dist/switch/NXSand.nro to sdmc:/switch/NXSand.nro. Run powershell -File scripts\verify-nro.ps1 before copying. Confirm the deployed NRO: delete sdmc:/switch/nxsand/launch.log, launch once, and check the latest block includes build: switch-sim-log-v11, switch: sim shader=sim.frag, romfs: sim.frag=… sim_rules_body.glsl=…, sim shader path: shaders/sim.frag, switch: default sim backend=fragment, and no preferring compute sim. Recopy from a fresh build-native.ps1 build if you still see sim_switch paths. If the app opens then exits, NXSand shows a fatal text screen and writes sdmc:/switch/nxsand/launch.log when possible. Overview Why it exists Serial interface and motion control daemon for Directed Perception PTU-46 precision pan-tilt robotic camera units.
Best fit Automated camera positioning for computer vision experiments.
Use cases Python 2 desktop and command-line tools that drive a PTU-46-17.5 pan-tilt unit over a serial port.
Use-case diagram for Pan-Tilt-Controller: Initialize the unit on start; Move to a pan/tilt position; Jog with arrows or buttons; Return to home position; Send raw serial commands Pan-Tilt-Controller Initialize the unit on start Move to a pan/tilt position Jog with arrows or buttons Return to home position Send raw serial commands Lab operator «system» PTU-46-17.5 unit People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Initialize the unit on start PTU-46-17.5 unit On start, pantiltcontroller.py opens COM3 at 9600 baud and sends speed, acceleration, reset, home position and pan and tilt limit commands (pxu1500, pnu-1000, tnu-850, txu585).
Move to a pan/tilt position Lab operatorPTU-46-17.5 unit The PyQt5 window in pantiltcontroller.py has Pan and Tilt fields; OK sends pp<value> and tp<value> and shows the unit's reply in a log box.
Jog with arrows or buttons Lab operatorPTU-46-17.5 unit The Control menu (Ctrl+O) opens a dialog whose arrow buttons, and the keyboard arrow keys, move pan or tilt by 5 positions per press.
Return to home position Lab operatorPTU-46-17.5 unit The Reset button sends pp0 and tp0 and sets the stored positions back to zero.
Send raw serial commands Lab operatorPTU-46-17.5 unit PTC-command.py is a prompt that forwards each typed line (for example r, pnu 1000, pp0) to the unit and prints the reply until exit is typed.
Scenario: Point the pan-tilt unit at a target Connect the PTU-46-17.5 to COM3 (the port is hard-coded) on a Windows PC with Python 2.7, pyserial, PyQt5 and pywin32.Run python pantiltcontroller.py; the script sets limits and moves the unit to 0,0.Type 500 in Pan and -200 in Tilt, then click OK.Open Control, Control and fine-tune with the arrow keys in steps of 5.Click Reset to bring the unit back to home. Overview Why it exists Sensor pixel analysis tool computing clipping histograms and dynamic range for RAW camera frames.
Best fit Camera sensor benchmarking and exposure verification in computational photography.
Use cases Python 2 scripts for camera-tuning engineers to check clipping, gamma and vignetting in raw Bayer sensor captures.
Use-case diagram for RawAnalyser: Mark ROI and gray patches; Analyse each new raw capture; Detect black or white clipping; Measure gamma and vignetting; Inspect one pixel's value; Convert raw files to TIFF RawAnalyser Mark ROI and gray patches Analyse each new raw capture Detect black or white clipping Measure gamma and vignetting Inspect one pixel's value Convert raw files to TIFF Image quality engineer «system» Camera capture folder People on the left, external systems on the right; each oval is a use case backed by the files cited below. Mark ROI and gray patches Image quality engineer GUI.py (PyQt5) opens a .raw or .tiff file, converts raw to TIFF for display and saves the clicked region of interest and gray patch corners to json/points.json.
Analyse each new raw capture Image quality engineerCamera capture folder RawAnalyser.py uses a watchdog observer on the given folder; every new 1928 x 1088 16-bit raw file is split into Bayer channels, saved as TIFF and analysed.
Detect black or white clipping Image quality engineer clipping() prints per-channel minimum and maximum 10-bit levels and flags CLIPPING BLACK or white in colour when values reach the sensor limits.
Measure gamma and vignetting Image quality engineer gamma() samples the gray patches from points.json; vignette() subtracts the black level (--bl, default 1024), divides by a stored .npy vignette map and writes a corrected TIFF.
Inspect one pixel's value Image quality engineer RawPixel.py prints the value and Bayer colour of the pixel at x, y for a given width, height and bit depth, and dumps channels to array/*.txt.
Convert raw files to TIFF Image quality engineerCamera capture folder Raw2Tiff.py writes a TIFF from one raw file; 20MPto5MP.py bins 20 MP OV20880 frames by summing 2 x 2 same-colour pixels into a 5 MP image.
Scenario: Check an OV2740 colour-checker capture Install Python 2.7 and the packages in requirements.txt, plus tifffile.Run python GUI.py, open a capture from raw/ and click the ROI and gray patches to update json/points.json.Start python RawAnalyser.py raw json/points.json --func basic --bl 1024 to watch the folder.Copy a new .raw capture into raw/; the script prints clipping warnings and gamma figures and writes a TIFF under tiff/.Check a suspicious spot with python RawPixel.py <file> x y --width 1928 --height 1088. Install RetroArch web build Self-hosterOnline file sources setup_retroarch.sh downloads the previous day's emscripten build from buildbot.libretro.com, extracts it into /var/www/html and unpacks the frontend bundle.
Download game sets Self-hosterOnline file sources InternetArchive.py (typer, rich, requests) scrapes the listed archive pages for .zip and .7z files in parallel and saves them under downloads/<system name>.
Sort games by first letter Self-hoster sort_mkdir.sh moves each file into a 0-9 or A-Z subfolder; the Dockerfile runs it for every Nintendo system folder.
Run the container Self-hoster docker-compose up -d builds the image and maps port 8080 to nginx; entrypoint.sh regenerates the .index-xhr file lists before starting nginx.
Play in the browser Browser player The player opens http://localhost:8080, picks a core and loads a game in the RetroArch Web Player page shipped with the nightly build (the repository keeps a copy as index.html, not copied by the Dockerfile).
Publish multi-arch images Self-hoster .github/workflows/retroarch-web-games.yaml builds with Docker Buildx for amd64, arm64 and arm/v7 and pushes antoinebou12/retroarch-web-games to Docker Hub.

Configure WriteTo.Sentry .NET developer SentrySinkExtensions.cs adds WriteTo.Sentry with a DSN and options such as environment, release, sampleRate, tags and enableTracing, usable from code or the Serilog section of appsettings.json.
Send logs and exceptions .NET developerSentry SentrySink.Emit maps the Serilog level, copies properties into scope extras and tags, adds breadcrumbs and calls CaptureMessage or CaptureException.
Trace each log as a span .NET developerSentry With enableTracing on, Emit starts a transaction named from the message template and a child span through ITransactionService, then finishes both.
Attach HTTP request context .NET developerSentry The AspNetCore package adds app.AddSentryContext() middleware and HttpContextDestructingPolicy so events carry the user, headers and request data.
Scrub data before sending .NET developer An optional beforeSend callback is chained after the sink's own handling; the SentryWeb demo also rewrites messages with a Serilog enricher (Scrubbing/DivisionByZeroFilter.cs).
Publish six NuGet packages NuGet.org .github/workflows/CI.yml packs the main, .6 and .10 package ids for net6.0 and net10.0 and pushes them to NuGet.org when a GitHub release is published.

The library is available on NuGet as Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK, or alternate ids Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK.6 / Serilog.Sinks.SentrySDK.10 if you want a single target framework per package. You can install it with the following command: This package references the Sentry NuGet package (6.3.2), the same major line as the Sentry for .NET documentation. For generic SDK setup (DSN, SendDefaultPii, debug), see the official Quick Start. Initialize the SDK as early as possible so startup failures are reported. It will not show lobbies published only in the desktop namespace. If a particular server rejects the Switch build, share switch-coopnet-identity.txt with that server’s operator; do not replace the genuine hash with another executable’s identity. Runtime diagnostics are written under switch/sm64coopdx/logs/, including startup.log, coopnet.log, checkpoints, and exception.log. When sharing diagnostics, remove lobby passwords, TURN credentials, and other private information first. Sign up and get a JWT API userMinIO S3 and MongoDB POST /auth/signup saves a user with hashed password and roles in MongoDB; POST /auth/signin returns a JwtResponse with the token and roles (AuthController.kt, JwtUtils.kt).
Upload a document Moderator or adminMinIO S3 and MongoDB POST /files/documents (moderator or admin) checks the extension against DOC_FILE_EXTENSION_REGEX, writes the bytes to the S3 bucket under files/<uuid>/<name> and records metadata in MongoDB.
Download a stored file API userMinIO S3 and MongoDB GET /files/{id} looks up the file record in MongoDB, reads the object from S3 and returns it as an attachment with its content type and size.
Manage Docker containers Moderator or admin The /containers routes list, create, start, stop, restart and rename containers through docker-java against the Docker host set in application.yml (tcp://127.0.0.1:2375).
Run a remote SSH command Moderator or admin POST /ssh/cli (admin only) opens an Apache SSHD session with the host, port and credentials in the request body and returns the command output.
Scenario: Store a PDF and fetch it back Start MongoDB on localhost:27017 and MinIO on localhost:9000, as configured in application.yml, then run ./gradlew bootRun.POST /auth/signup with a username, email, password and the role "mod".POST /auth/signin and copy the JWT from the response.POST /files/documents with the PDF in the multipart field "document" and the Bearer token; the response returns fileId and fileName.GET /files/{fileId} to download the PDF, or browse the routes in Swagger UI at /api-docs. Check the Wi-Fi link Switch ownerHorizon NIFM / BTM The Dashboard tab reads link type, SSID, IPv4, gateway, DNS and 0-3 signal bars from NIFM through NetworkService, with RSSI from legacy wlan:inf only where firmware exposes it.
Benchmark the connection Switch ownerHTTPS speed server SpeedTestEngine runs 8 HTTPS latency probes, then a 25 MiB download and a 10 MiB zero-filled upload with libcurl against speed.cloudflare.com by default, reporting median, P95 and jitter.
Review saved networks Switch ownerHorizon NIFM / BTM The Networks tab lists basic saved-profile metadata and Horizon's allowed channels, with channel-overlap math from core/metrics; credentials are never read for display.
Scan Bluetooth state Switch ownerHorizon NIFM / BTM BluetoothService reads BTM radio state and device counts, and runs a bounded passive BLE scan that returns at most ten unique addresses.
Export a diagnostics report Switch owner The About tab writes sdmc:/switch-wifi-diagnostics.txt with the app version, compatibility target, network details and Bluetooth counts, without credentials.

Keep Horizon/libnx IPC out of the Borealis UI layer. Add a host-side test for calculations and parsers whenever possible. Gate firmware-dependent behavior explicitly. Do not call a derived AP-overlap value “noise floor”, “SNR”, or “channel utilization” unless the underlying metric is actually measured. Keep Bluetooth diagnostics read-only. Render one diagram MCP client (AI chat)Kroki / PlantUML generate_uml takes a diagram_type, the source code, a format and an optional theme, renders through Kroki (KROKI_SERVER, https://kroki.io by default) and returns the file, its URL and a playground link.
Validate diagram source MCP client (AI chat) validate_uml checks the type, format and basic structure locally without rendering, so the assistant can fix the source before calling a renderer.
Render a batch of diagrams MCP client (AI chat)Kroki / PlantUML generate_uml_batch renders several items with bounded concurrency and stable ordering, up to the batch_max_items setting.
Edit in the chat viewer DeveloperMCP client (AI chat) In clients that support MCP Apps, results open in ui://uml-mcp/diagram-viewer, where the user can zoom, edit the source, change theme or format and export SVG, PNG, HTML or PDF.
Self-host the server DeveloperKroki / PlantUML uv tool install uml-mcp && uml-mcp setup installs it locally; docker-compose.yml starts the server on port 8000 with Kroki containers and an opt-in PlantUML fallback profile, and deploy/helm/uml-mcp targets Kubernetes.

Overview Why it exists TypeScript dictionary validation and game solver engine supporting multiple languages and word lengths.
Best fit Algorithmic word game logic and solver heuristics.

Guess a five-letter word Player The /phil page (MotDuJourPhilPage/App.tsx) gives six tries on a 6×5 grid, rejects words missing from the French list in data/fr.ts and colours letters and keyboard keys; the solution is hard-coded to GRAND.
Create an account Player /signup, /login, /forgot-password and /reset-password use Redwood dbAuth (api/src/functions/auth.ts) against the User model with hashed password and salt.
Manage words and word banks Administrator Routes under /admin, wrapped in Private roles="admin", give scaffolded CRUD pages for users, languages, words, word banks, games, try rows, letters and statistics through the GraphQL SDL services.
Seed French words AdministratorOnline dictionaries yarn seed runs scripts/seed.ts, which upserts languages and the fr word bank, then fetches definitions from fr.wiktionary.org or le-dictionnaire.com with the cheerio crawler before inserting words.
Track games and streaks Player The Prisma schema stores each Game with its TryRow and Letter records and a Statistic row per user (games played, won, lost, streak, average); the data model is in place but the play pages do not write to it yet.
Scenario: Run the French board locally Start PostgreSQL with docker run --name=db -e POSTGRES_USER=admin -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=admin -p 5432:5432 -d postgres, as in the root README.In WordsEnigma/, run yarn install, then yarn rw prisma migrate dev to apply api/db/migrations.Run yarn seed to load the languages, the fr word bank and the words.Start yarn redwood dev and open http://localhost:8910/phil.Type five letters, press Enter and read the colours until the word is found or the six rows are used. HDR-10bpp-Display-Test HDR-10bpp-Display-Test checks HDR 4K display on Linux, including 10 bits per channel. Useful for validating the graphics stack, drivers, and monitor.
Getting Started HDR-10bpp-Display-Test: A test project for HDR 4K display on Linux.
Prerequisites Before running the test, ensure your system has the following software installed:
X server Python 3 GTK 3 ImageJ (for 10-bit color depth image display) ImageIO (for reading image files) On Ubuntu or Debian-based systems, install these packages using the command:
sudo apt-get install xserver-xorg python3 python3-gi python3-gi-cairo gir1.2-gtk-3.0 imagej Installing ImageIO is a necessary component and can be installed via pip:
pip3 install imageio Running the Test To conduct the test, follow these steps:
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/HDR-10bpp-Display-Test.git Navigate to the project directory:
cd HDR-10bpp-Display-Test Stop the display manager and X server:
sudo systemctl stop lightdm || sudo systemctl stop gdm sudo pkill Xorg Start the X server with a color depth of 30:
startx -- -depth 30 Verify the X server’s color depth:
xwininfo -root | grep Depth Launch the viewer application:
python3 Viewer.py python3 Viewer3.py # for video support To display an image, use:
imagej --no-splash /path/to/image Check if the image is displayed correctly with accurate colors.
Troubleshooting If the X server fails to start with a color depth of 30, attempt to start it with a depth of 24 instead:
startx -- -depth 24 License This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE.md file for details.
summary: A test to verify HDR 4K display on Linux with 10-bit color depth.
title: HDR-10bpp-Display-Test

RawAnalyser RawAnalyser is a Python tool for analyzing raw images: black and white clipping detection, gamma calculation, and flatness with vignette detection (Algolux).
Prerequisites You need to have Python 2.7 installed and the following libraries:
json time numpy scipy pyqt5 argparse argcomplete watchdog logging colorama plotly matplotlib Usage Run the RawAnalyser script: python RawAnalyser.py <pathfolder> <pointfile> --func <clipping,gamma,vignette,histogram,noHist,basic, default all> --bl <black level, default 1024> --vignette <pathvignette> Start the GUI: python GUI.py Check the value of the pixel and the color with the bayer pattern: python RawPixel.pt input<file> x y --bitdepth <8,10,16,default 16> Scripts Description RawAnalyser.py Checks black and white clipping levels in a raw image. Takes a folder path and a JSON file with the region of interest and gray patches.
points.json The JSON file specifying the region of interest. An example of its structure is as follows:
{ "last_y": 798, "last_x": 1353, "gray_first_y": 691, "gray_first_x": 606, "first_x": 603, "first_y": 315, "gray_last_x": 1347, "gray_last_y": 795 } GUI.py A GUI script for image selection. It allows you to select the region of interest and the gray patches in a raw or TIFF file, which are then saved in a JSON file. It also constantly checks for new files in the raw folder.
RawPixel.py A script to inspect the value of a specific pixel and determine its color using the Bayer pattern.
20MPto5MP.py Converts 20-megapixel images to 5-megapixel images for the OV20880 sensor.
Camera Example of camera sensor information:
Camera: OV2740 Resolution: (1088, 1928) ImageType: BINARY16U Sensor value: 10 bit Bayer pattern: 'bggr'
summary: Python tool for raw image analysis: clipping, gamma, vignette, and Bayer pixel inspection.
title: RawAnalyser
